messages:
Sam: heads-up — ACME Ads reported p99 for /v1/embeddings on dedicated-usw2 jumped from ~500ms to ~1.9s starting ~02:10 PDT (after last-night node driver rollout). customer is seeing production regressions, they escalated to support.
Maria: I can see corresponding host-level iowait spikes on a subset of dedicated nodes (ded-usw2-gpupool-3*). KV cache miss rate also increased. quick check: rolling driver + kernel preempt window might have changed I/O scheduling.
Ryan: logs: kernel blk stats show nvme qdepth spikes and high queue_time_ms on those nodes. snapshot: `iostat -x 1 5` shows %util ~98 and await increasing. nvme-cli shows heavy flushes.
Priya: repro steps I ran from our test harness: small batch embed calls (n=4, seq_len=128) to model redwood/embedding-compact on those nodes -> p95 stable but p99 a lot higher and tail is correlated with host fs flushes.
Sam: posting curl repro payload for on-call to repro quickly:

curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/embeddings"
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY"
 -d '{"model":"redwood/embedding-compact","input":["foo","bar","baz","qux"]}'

Maria: quick mitigation I applied: cordoned two noisy nodes from the dedicated pool and shifted traffic to other nodes (autoscale handled capacity). immediate p99 dropped from ~1.9s -> ~650ms for affected customer.
Ryan: investigative note: kernel pagecache background writeback frequency increased after a host kernel config change we rolled with the driver update (vm.dirty_ratio/dirty_background_ratio tuned). Combined with NVMe flushes from KV cache eviction, we got short-lived hostfs stalls.
Priya: workaround we tested: lower vm.dirty_ratio to 5 and reduce dirty_background_ratio to 2 on affected hosts, and temporarily increased kvcache retention for embeddings to reduce eviction churn. both helped reduce host I/O bursts in repro.
Sam: action items:
- short: keep cordon on 2 noisy nodes, route customer traffic to stable nodes, communicate ETA to ACME Ads (support-liaison)
- medium: revert kernel tuning on the pool and push vm.* changes as safe rollback (eng-infra)
- long: vendor/driver follow-up and a proper root-cause doc
ops-bot: scheduled job run: `ansible -i ded-usw2 hosts -m sysctl -a` queued, will apply vm.dirty_ratio=5 when approved.
support-liaison: I messaged ACME: "we've identified host-level I/O interference on a small set of reserved nodes after a maintenance update. we've shifted your traffic and expect improved p99 within the hour. follow-up report incoming." :thumbsup:
Maria: additional probe — I ran a tight single-node loop with `fio` randsync writes and saw host stall patterns correlate with embedding requests. suggests interference between logging/writeback and NVMe queuing.
Ryan: temporary mitigation we pushed to prod routing: prefer nodes with lower kernel writeback settings for embedding-heavy routes, and enable prefix KV-cache sticky pins for this customer to reduce cross-tenant evictions.
Priya: remediation checklist being drafted: kernel param rollback PR, kvcache retention tweak, and a driver vendor support ticket with traces attached (blkq tracepoints + nvme telemetry). I'll attach repro traces to the ticket.
Sam: does anyone object to scheduling a driver rollback window tonight for the dedicated pool if vendor analysis doesn't show quick fix?
Maria: +1 from infra side, but need to coordinate with capacity ops (we'll do gradual rollback and monitor p99).
support-liaison: ACME asked for a postmortem and ETA. I'll confirm rollback plan window and update them.
Ryan: note for postmortem: include command snippets and script used to collect nvme/blk traces, e.g., `echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/events/block/trace/enable` and `nvme telemetry get-log`.
Priya: I'll start composing the incident doc and include repro commands, the sysctl changes we tested, and the kvcache config diff.
Sam: thanks team — keep thread updated. tagging eng-infra and eng-runtime for visibility. :pulse_railway_track:
